This installer has not yet run on any device. Every device step is unverified until lab test Q-INST-06 is certified.
Rendered offline, without reading the device. Before unit 1, check that your CLI prompt shows labadmin@<the lab device you intend>, and do every STOP check ('show system commit', 'show | compare'): nothing here knows what the device already has.
LAB ONLY. This adds 'set system scripts language python3'. That lets any unsigned Python script owned by a super-user-class account run on this device's routing engine, not only J-Wicket: a change to the device's security posture. J-Wicket is not qualified for production (gate G1 has not passed). Continue only on a disposable lab device you are allowed to change.
With --access tunnel, J-Wicket listens on 127.0.0.1 only and is reached through 'ssh -L', which needs SSH TCP forwarding on the device. On a lab SRX4100 running Junos 25.2R1-S1.4 the tunnel was refused ('administratively prohibited') and 'set system services ssh tcp-forwarding' is a syntax error there (verified, docs/evidence/2026-11-24-srx4100-lab). The SRX configuration schema at 23.2R1 marks tcp-forwarding deprecated and names 'set system services ssh allow-tcp-forwarding'; that statement was not tried (unverified, Q-NET-03). Health check C8 is not available with this mode. --access tls is the alternative.
J-Wicket will run with the rights of labadmin, a super-user-class account that can commit configuration ('username labadmin' under 'system extensions extension-service application file jwicket.py'). A compromise of J-Wicket is a compromise of this device.
In an SSH or console session on the lab device (the shell is outside Juniper support; this is the one read the installers make there):
Unit 1 (device-shell): veriexec state
Status: verified (spike ran exactly this command; 'loaded active enforce' also on SRX4100 25.2R1-S1.4)
```
start shell sh
sysctl security.mac.veriexec.state
exit
```
STOP unless it printed 'loaded active enforce'. Otherwise results from this device are not qualification evidence.

Unit 2 (device-operational): pending commits and the state directory
Status: commands documented (F10, CMT-01); not recorded on a device; output shapes unverified (Q-INST-01)
```
show system commit | no-more
file list /var/db detail
file list /var/db/scripts/jet detail
```
STOP if, in 'show system commit', the newest entry (0) ends with 'commit confirmed, rollback in <n>mins' (a commit confirmed is waiting) or the output starts with 'commit requested by' (a pending 'commit at'); Juniper's sample wording, unverified on 24.4 (Q-INST-01).
In 'file list /var/db detail', jwicket must be listed as 'drwx------' and 'labadmin'. If it is absent or listed otherwise, do unit 3 (once, as root), then paste this unit again.

J-Wicket keeps its settings in /var/db/jwicket, and that directory is absent or J-Wicket cannot trust it: it must be a real directory, not a symbolic link, owned by labadmin, mode 700, so that 'file list /var/db detail' shows 'drwx------' and 'labadmin'. A super-user-class account cannot create it: on a lab SRX4100 running Junos 25.2R1-S1.4 both 'mkdir' and 'file make-directory' were refused with 'Permission denied' (verified). The installer never creates it, never logs in as root and never asks for the root password, and it writes nothing while the directory is not right. Once, in a shell on the lab device as root (outside Juniper support; how you become root is your lab's own procedure), run 'mkdir -m 700 /var/db/jwicket && chown labadmin /var/db/jwicket' (docs/deploy-lab.md step 3; root's directory and chown were verified on that SRX4100, the '-m 700' mode is inferred), then run the installer again. If 'file list /var/db detail' lists jwicket as a symbolic link (its permissions start with 'l'), first remove the link itself, as root, with 'rm /var/db/jwicket' (never 'rm -r'), because chmod and chown change a link's target. If it is a real directory with another owner or mode, run instead, as root, 'chmod 700 /var/db/jwicket && chown labadmin /var/db/jwicket' (unverified). Moving the settings file elsewhere is an owner decision, not a lab workaround.
Only if unit 2 did not list jwicket as 'drwx------' and 'labadmin', in a shell on the lab device as root:
Unit 3 (device-shell): the state directory, once, as root
Status: verified on SRX4100 25.2R1-S1.4 as root (the command: docs/deploy-lab.md step 3; that root made the directory: docs/evidence/2026-11-24-srx4100-lab); outside Juniper support; how you become root is your lab's own procedure
```
mkdir -m 700 /var/db/jwicket && chown labadmin /var/db/jwicket
```
Leave the root shell, and in your own session paste unit 2 again: jwicket must now be listed as 'drwx------' and 'labadmin'. The installers never do this step and never ask for the root password.

Save these lines on the workstation as jwicket.ini:
Unit 5 (file): the settings file (workstation) [file jwicket.ini]
Status: render_settings output; parsed by jwicket.settings in the tests
```
# /var/db/jwicket/jwicket.ini: J-Wicket settings, written by jwicket-install (lab only).
# Every value is checked before anything listens. J-Wicket listens on 127.0.0.1 only and is
# reached through an SSH tunnel (--access tunnel); run the installer again to change this file.

[server]
bind = 127.0.0.1
port = 8443
allowed_hosts = 127.0.0.1:8443, localhost:8443

[auth]
backend = lab-token
lab_token_file = /var/db/jwicket/lab-token

[log]
file = /var/db/jwicket/jwicket.log
audit_file = /var/db/jwicket/audit.jsonl
```

Unit 6 (workstation): copy the settings (workstation)
Status: scp -O verified (spike); the lab-token lines from deploy-lab's variant (not in the recorded results)
```
chmod 600 jwicket.ini
scp -O jwicket.ini labadmin@<device>:/var/db/jwicket/jwicket.ini
(umask 077 && openssl rand -hex 24 > lab-token)
chmod 600 lab-token
scp -O lab-token labadmin@<device>:/var/db/jwicket/lab-token
rm lab-token
```

Unit 7 (device-operational): check the files

If a mode is wrong: 'file change-permission /var/db/scripts/jet/jwicket.py permission 644' (and the same for the others); outside Juniper support, the shell's 'chmod' does the same.

Unit 9B (device-configuration): stage diagnostics: the configuration change
Status: 'load set <file>' documented (verified); a relative name loading from the home directory inferred
```
load set jwicket-diagnostics.set
show | compare | no-more
```
STOP unless 'show | compare' shows the same statements and nothing else. This rendering does not know which levels the device already has: Junos prints each change under the deepest level that already exists, and a new level (for example a new 'file jwicket.py' entry) as a braced block of '+' lines under that header, so the same statements may appear grouped that way rather than one leaf per header (illustrative; real samples are recorded by lab test Q-INST-01). For example:
    [edit system extensions extension-service application file jwicket_probe.py]
    +    username labadmin;
    [edit system extensions extension-service application file jwicket_probe.py checksum]
    +    sha-256 1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f;
    [edit system extensions extension-service application file jwicket_selftest.py]
    +    username labadmin;
    [edit system extensions extension-service application file jwicket_selftest.py checksum]
    +    sha-256 1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f1f;
    [edit system scripts]
    +    language python3;
If the comparison does not list 'language python3', it was already set: that is fine.
If it shows anything else, type 'rollback 0' and 'exit'.

Compare with what each check expects:
C4: Exactly one new 'listening on <address>:8443' line in /var/db/jwicket/jwicket.log since the commit ('file show /var/db/jwicket/jwicket.log'); two mean a restart loop.
    expect exactly one new line containing: listening on 127.0.0.1:8443 tls=False backend=lab-token routing_instance=default version=0.1.0.dev1 payload=2e2e2e2e2e2e2e2e
C5: Exactly one new audit record with event start and this bundle's version in /var/db/jwicket/audit.jsonl.
C6: No new /var/db/jwicket/startup-refused.txt (a stale one is deleted before the commit).
    expect an error saying the file does not exist
C7: 'show extension-service status jwicket.py' shows the same process id at two reads at least 30 seconds apart.
C8: --access tls: an HTTPS GET /api/session from the workstation to <address>:8443, trusting only the certificate whose SHA-256 the installer generated (pinned: no CA store, and the pin stands in for the host name check), answers 200 with this version (and build). --access tunnel: not available (no check uses an SSH channel).
    not available with --access tunnel: no check uses an SSH channel (forwarding was refused on SRX4100 25.2R1-S1.4)
C10: Before confirming: the committed statements of the touched subtrees equal the plan, and the committed delta ('show | compare rollback 1') changes nothing outside them.
    expect 'show | compare rollback 1' to show only the change of unit B

    expect the newest commit by labadmin with the comment: jwicket 0.1.0.dev1 sha256:1f1f1f1f1f1f runtime lab-install

Unit 11 (workstation): open the UI through an SSH tunnel (workstation)
Status: explicit 127.0.0.1 bind (INV-10); SSH forwarding refused on SRX4100 25.2R1-S1.4 (verified)
```
ssh -L 127.0.0.1:8443:127.0.0.1:8443 labadmin@<device>
```
Then browse to http://127.0.0.1:8443/ while the SSH session stays open.

Health check C8 is not available with this mode. --access tls is the alternative.
